title: Ocean or Land Checker: Is This Point Water?
description: Check whether coordinates fall on ocean or land with the Ocean or Land Checker — a reverse-geocode read of the point's record. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a point at 0°, 0° — the famous null island of data errors — answers as ocean with no address at all, and half the world's broken geocoding pipelines are discovered by exactly that silence.
quick_answer: The Ocean or Land Checker reverse-geocodes a point to tell whether map data treats it as land with an address or as sparse ocean. Paste coordinates or click the map and read the result: a land-style record with place fields, or the empty signature of open water.

faq: Is it a survey shoreline?
No — the checker reads the reverse-geocode record: land-style fields versus ocean's sparsity. It is exact about what the data says and honest that data and coastline are cousins, not twins.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — paste or click any coordinates on earth.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Shorelines are drawn at different resolutions by different sources; a point metres from a coast can flip verdicts between maps.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No.
A point on land returned nothing.
Sparse-data land (deserts, deep interiors, some islands) can read empty. The map view is the tie-breaker — the checker reports the record, not the terrain.
Lakes and rivers?
Inland water usually resolves to the surrounding land record or a water name, varying by data. It is not the ocean, and the record generally says so one way or another.
Antarctica?
Land — with a research-station style record in places, and glorious emptiness elsewhere. The verdict 'land' holds either way.
Why do pipelines send points to 0,0?
Missing coordinates default to zero in many systems. The checker is the bouncer that catches them at the door.
Tides change the answer?
The record's shoreline is fixed at its survey state; a tidal flat point keeps the record's verdict at all tides. Boats should consult charts, not this checker.
Coordinates from a photo?
Paste them — EXIF positions are exactly the forensic use case. Remember some platforms strip EXIF; the original file keeps it.
